newsitem.title: EGYPT: Cairo schools closed for fear of meningitis.
newsitem.headline: Cairo schools closed for fear of meningitis.

text.p: Schools in a south Cairo suburb have been closed for several days after a pair of twins died of meningitis, residents said on Monday.
"Thirteen-year-old Michael and his twin sister died after being infected by the meningitis virus," one of their close acquaintances said.
"Doctors privately admitted it was meningitis and were treating them accordingly," she added. "But the official report did not concede it."
In a televised news conference on Sunday Health Minister Ismail Sallam dismissed the reports as a rumour, saying the deaths were a result of a brain virus.
The ministry, however, ordered schools in the luxurious Cairo suburb of Maadi closed for two days "just to reassure parents". Residents said the schools would be closed until the weekend.
Other cases from Maadi schools have been admitted to intensive care and vaccines have disappeared after a rush by scared parents, residents said.
